transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

What brings me in is… well, when I know I have to cross a bridge, I get frightened right away. Before I’m even on it, my heart starts pounding, my hands get damp on the steering wheel or the armrest, and I feel this awful rush of fear. It’s gotten bad enough that I thought I should talk to someone.
Is it only bridges that trigger this fear, or are there other situations or places that cause a similar reaction?

It’s mostly bridges—especially high ones. I can tell myself, logically, that cars go over them all day and nothing happens. But if I see one coming up on the map or through the windshield, it feels like the whole span is just going to drop out from under us.
Do you experience a similar fear when you're in other high places, like tall buildings or balconies?
I’m not really sure. I don’t spend much time on balconies or in tall buildings these days. The thing I’ve really noticed is the bridges.
Do you feel anxious or fearful when you are in high places other than bridges?
I honestly don’t know. I don’t really put myself in those situations much, so I can’t say for sure. The bridge situation is the one I’m clear about.
Have you ever been in a situation where you were in a high place, other than a bridge, and felt a fear similar to what you experience when approaching a bridge?
I can’t really think of a time like that. I don’t go up in high places much anymore, so I haven’t had a clear situation to compare it to. The bridges are the thing I know brings it on.
Do you think your fear would decrease if you were crossing the bridge on foot rather than in a vehicle?

I don’t think it would make much difference. I know plenty of cars go over those bridges every day, and they’re probably safe, but when I see a high span coming up, or even on the map, it feels like the whole thing could drop away under me. Whether I’m walking or in a car, that thought is still there.
Would you say your fear is specifically of bridges, or is it more about the height of the bridge that scares you?

It’s more the height of the bridge, I think. I know thousands of cars cross them every day, but when I see a high span coming up, or even just on a map, it feels like the whole thing could drop away under us.
Would your fear be less intense if you were standing at the edge of a high cliff, rather than on a bridge?

I’m not sure it would be the same. With a bridge, it’s that high span itself—seeing it ahead or even on a map—and I know cars go over it every day, but it still feels like it could just drop away underneath us. A cliff might bother me too, but the bridge is what really sets that off for me.
Would you feel afraid if you were on a ladder or some other high, but not bridge-like, structure?

Maybe a little, but it’s not really the same thing for me. The thing that gets me is a high bridge—when I see it coming up through the windshield, or even notice it on a map. I know lots of people cross those bridges every day, but it still feels like it could just drop away underneath us.
Would your fear of heights be triggered by being on a high floor of a building, even if you're not directly near a window or edge?

I don’t think just being on a high floor, away from the window, would do it the same way. What really gets me is seeing a high bridge coming up, or even seeing it on a map. I know plenty of cars cross those every day, but it feels like it could drop away under us.
Would your fear be triggered by being in other types of elevated structures, such as an elevated walkway or an overpass, that are not bridges?

I don’t know about every kind of elevated thing. What I can say is, with a high bridge, I know perfectly well thousands of cars go over it every day, but when I see that high span on a map or coming up through the windshield, it feels like the whole thing is just waiting to drop away under us.
Would you feel afraid if you were on an elevated walkway that is not a bridge?

I’m not really sure about an elevated walkway. What I know is the high bridges are what do it. I can tell myself thousands of cars go over them every day, but when I see one on the map or coming up ahead through the windshield, it feels like it could just drop away under us.
Would your fear of bridges decrease if you couldn't see the water or ground below while crossing?

I’m not sure it would make much difference. It isn’t only seeing the water or the ground. Even when I see the high span on a map or coming up through the windshield, I know cars cross it all day, but it still feels like the whole thing could drop away under us.
Would you feel afraid if you were on a similar elevated structure, like an overpass, that is not directly over water?

I’m not sure about an overpass specifically. What I do know is that with those high spans, even though I know cars go over them all day long, once I see it on the map or coming up through the windshield, I get this feeling like it could just drop away underneath us.
Would you feel afraid if you were on a ferris wheel?

I don’t really know. I haven’t been on a Ferris wheel in a long time, and I can’t say for sure how I’d react. My trouble is more with certain high bridges, not something I’ve noticed with Ferris wheels.
Would you feel afraid if you were on a platform or a ledge that is high off the ground but not a bridge?
I’m not really sure. I don’t spend time on high ledges or platforms, so I can’t say how I’d react. The thing I know bothers me is those high bridges.
Would you feel afraid if you were in a tall building with a glass floor that allows you to see the ground far below?
I can’t really say. I don’t think I’ve been in a place like that, with a glass floor looking straight down. What I know is it’s those high bridges that set me off.
Would you feel afraid if you were in a closed, elevated space like an upper floor of a building with no view of the ground outside?
I don’t think so, but I’m not completely sure. If I’m just on an upper floor and I can’t see down, I haven’t really noticed feeling afraid from that alone.
Would you feel afraid if you were in a closed, elevated space like an airplane during flight?
I’m not sure about that. I don’t fly much anymore, and I can’t say I’ve noticed being afraid just because the plane is up high and enclosed.
